html:
The Zhou dynasty was the royal house of China from about 1046 to 256 BCE, the longest of any Chinese dynasty. Its kings ruled in fact only for the first part of that time; afterwards they reigned in name while rival states fought for power.

The Zhou came from the Wei River valley in the west. King Wu defeated the Shang at the Battle of Muye around 1046 BCE. His brother, the Duke of Zhou, secured the new state. The Zhou explained their victory with the Mandate of Heaven: Heaven gives the right to rule to a virtuous house and takes it away from a wicked one. Chinese dynasties used this idea for three thousand years.

The periods:

  • Western Zhou, about 1046 to 771 BCE: the kings ruled from the west and gave land to relatives and allies as lords of their own states.
  • 771 BCE: the capital was sacked and the court moved east to Luoyi, near modern Luoyang.
  • Spring and Autumn period, 771 to about 481 BCE: the king lost real power; great lords competed.
  • Warring States period, about 475 to 221 BCE: seven big states fought total wars with mass infantry armies.

Political chaos came with a burst of thought, the "Hundred Schools". Confucius, Laozi, Mencius, Mozi and the Legalists all lived in Eastern Zhou times. Bronze work reached its peak, iron tools spread, and coins came into use.

The state of Qin ended the last Zhou king in 256 BCE and unified China in 221 BCE.
sum: The Zhou dynasty was the royal house of China from about 1046 to 256 BCE, the longest of any Chinese dynasty. Its kings ruled in fact only for the first part of that time; afterwards they reigned in name while rival states fought for power.
